A Division Bench comprising Justices Debangsu Basak and Aryak Dutt passed the ruling on a habeas corpus petition seeking the accused worker’s release. “We hold the period of detention of the writ petitioner between August 6, 2018 and October 5, 2018 was not sanctioned by law. The writ petitioner, therefore, is entitled to compensation for such period,” the October 5 ruling said. Justices Debangsu Basak, Aryak Dutt The worker (petitioner) had been booked in three criminal cases, but had secured bail in all of them and was supposed to be released from jail on August 6, 2018. However, he was not immediately released, prompting him to file a petition before the High Court for release. He was later released on October 5, 2018, around 2 months after he was supposed to be released on bail. His counsel told the High Court that he was entitled to compensation of ₹20 lakhs for the 60-day period that he was illegally detained for. The State claimed that the petitioner remained in custody in connection with this MR case till October 5, 2018. items.title: Allahabad High Court applies US doctrine of 'fruit of poisonous tree' to release accused arrested after illegal detention
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently ordered release of an accused who was formally arrested by the police on September 16 only after keeping him under illegal detention for 31 hours [Ravi Chaurasiya And Another v State of UP and 4 others] A bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdeva found that the police formally arrested the accused Ravi Chaurasiya only after his mother approached the High Court with a habeas corpus petition. Prior to that, he was being kept in illegal detention. “The police cannot be permitted to legitimize an arrest, where it was subsequent to an act of unlawful detention. The subsequent arrest memo and the remand does not legitimize the initial unlawful detention of the corpus. Therefore, where the initial action of unlawful detention itself was violative of the right of the corpus under Article 22, the same cannot be set right by a subsequent action of the police by formally arresting the corpus on 16.09.2026 at 10.45 am,” the Court ruled. The Court rejected the police claim that they forgot to make an entry in the General Diary for Chaurasiya's custody for more than 24 hours. It noted that he was arrested for being the purchaser of a property belonging to a gangster. The Court directed Chaurasiya's release and also ordered the Commissioner of Prayagraj to conduct an inquiry into the matter, particularly, the conduct of the Station House Officer (SHO). “This Court records its displeasure with regard to the conduct of the S.H.O. of Police Station Soraon. If, in the inquiry conducted against the deponent, the Commissioner is satisfied that there has been negligence on his part, in such an eventuality, the displeasure which is recorded in this order, be entered in his service record,” it directed. Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev While considering Chaurasiya’s plea to release him in the case, the Court examined the doctrine of ‘fruit of poisonous tree’ in the context of his illegal detention, which was subsequently formalised by producing him before a magistrate. Fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine, which originated in the United States of America, is a doctrine which prohibits the appreciation of any evidence gathered unlawfully. “In the case under judgment, this Court examined the Fruit of the Poisonous Tree doctrine, not in the context of the law of evidence, but in its application to constitutional law, with specific reference to civil liberties protected under Part III of the Constitution of India. items.title: 281 lawyers apply for Senior Advocate designation under Madras High Court's new Rules
items.summary: 281 lawyers practicing before the Madras High Court have applied for Senior Advocate designation under a substantially revamped designation regime. The High Court on October 6 published the list of applicants and invited suggestions or views from practising advocates, the Bar Council and relevant bar associations. The views must be supported by verifiable material and should be submitted to the Registrar (Administration) by 5.45 pm on October 27. The list runs to 281 applicants, with enrolment years ranging from the 1970s to 2015. The exercise comes nearly four years after the High Court's previous round of designations. In January 2023, the full court of the High Court designated 62 lawyers as Senior Advocates under the then-existing 2020 Rules. The present exercise, however, is being conducted under the Rules for Designation of Senior Advocates by the High Court of Madras, 2026. The news Rules were notified on July 23 this year. The new Rules were framed against the backdrop of a May 2025 Supreme Court judgment that discarded the earlier 100-point assessment system for Senior Advocate designations and directed High Courts to amend or substitute their existing rules. The Madras High Court's 2026 Rules consequently do away with the earlier points-based assessment and interview system. The full court is to assess candidates on their ability, standing at the bar and special knowledge or experience in law. items.title: Bulli Bai case: Mumbai Court discharges accused Vishal Jha; says merely following mobile app no offence
items.summary: A Mumbai court has closed the case Vishal Sudhirkumar Jha in the Bulli Bai app case in which photographs of over 100 Muslim women were displayed for an auction [Vishal Jha v. State of Maharashtra] The judicial magistrate at Bandra RT Ingle passed the order on October 6. The magistrate highlighted the lack of direct involvement of Jha and ruled that merely being in contact with co-accused does not automatically establish liability for their criminal acts. “May be the applicant has followed Bullibai App due to his familiarity with the co-accused and contact with them, but, in entire charge-sheet there is no further role of the present applicant which would show that, he either created said App or the help co-accused in creating it,” the judge said. The judge also relied on an Allahabad High Court precedent to establish that simply following a page on a website is not a punishable offence. The case revolves around an application hosted on GitHub that unlawfully displayed photographs of over 100 Muslim women for an intended auction. Jha and two other accused had previously secured bail on April 12 after the court observed that older co-accused had abused their immaturity. This decision marks the first official discharge in the prominent cybercrime investigation. Jha was facing charges under Sections 153(a) (promoting enmity between different groups), 153(b) (imputations prejudicial to national integration), and 295(a) (deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings) alongside Section 67 of the Information Technology Act for publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form. Advocate Aarati Deshmukh for Jha argued for discharge on the grounds that the charge-sheet failed to make out any offence against Jha, as his only alleged action was following the app. She argued that the investigating officer could not produce evidence demonstrating that Jha shared the application on his Twitter account as claimed. The court accepted the arguments and discharged him from all charges. Additional Public Prosecutor Kalpana Hire appeared for State. [Read order]

Sagar Rathod & Anr. ]. A Bench of Justices Urmila Joshi-Phalke and Raj D Wakode ruled that threatening judicial officers and shouting inside a courtroom constituted grave misconduct. Obstruction in the judicial process by lawyers cannot be tolerated under any circumstances, the Court underscored. “Interference in the administration of justice by giving threats, addressing the judicial officer in loud voice and prohibiting him from passing orders are definitely serious acts. More so, when such acts have been done by an advocate who is the officer of the Court, he should promote and see that all others who are present should also maintain the decorum of the Court. Obstruction in judicial process by an advocate cannot be tolerated,” the Court held. The Bench further stressed that belated or insincere excuses cannot erase contemptuous conduct. items.title: Coimbatore hospital drops Hindi from medicine covers after DMK leader’s criticism
items.summary: The Coimbatore Medical College Hospital (CMCH) on Tuesday, October 6, replaced medicine covers carrying instructions in Hindi, Tamil, and English after the covers triggered a row over Tamil Nadu’s two-language policy. The move came after Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader and former Industries Minister TRB Rajaa criticised the use of Hindi on the covers, saying it appeared that a three-language policy was being implemented in government hospitals. Similar covers had also been used at the Government Medical College Hospital in Karur, which has also stopped using them. According to CMCH resident medical officer B Saravanapriya, the covers were not newly introduced and had been in use for more than 18 months, including under the previous government. “These covers are being printed at Chinthamani Cooperative Society with funds from sponsors,” she told The Times of India. The hospital has instructed pharmacists to stop using the trilingual covers and switch to new covers containing only Tamil and English. Staff have also been told to manually stamp dosage instructions on plain covers and fill them in according to each patient’s prescription before handing over medicines. The printed instructions were used to indicate when and how often medicines should be taken. However, pharmacists at CMCH have raised concerns that removing the Hindi instructions could make it harder for migrant workers who do not understand Tamil or English to follow their prescriptions. Pharmacists also pointed to an existing manpower shortage, saying that explaining dosage instructions individually to such patients would take additional time. CMCH handles around 3,000 to 4,500 outpatients every day, including a significant number of migrant workers from Coimbatore and surrounding areas. Rajaa had posted photographs of the medicine covers on X, writing, “It seems like the three-language policy is being implemented in Tamil Nadu hospitals too! First Karur... Now the same situation in Coimbatore as well.” The controversy first surfaced after photographs of similar covers from the Government Medical College Hospital in Karur appeared on social media. The covers carried dosage instructions in Tamil, English, and Hindi, prompting criticism from DMK leaders, including Pudukottai MLA V Muthuraja, who questioned the use of Hindi and linked it to the wider debate over Tamil Nadu’s language policy. The Gandhi siblings staged a prolonged sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan after police stopped the Opposition’s march from Parliament towards the Election Commission of India (ECI) headquarters. The protest ended after Rahul and Priyanka, along with several INDIA bloc leaders, were removed from the premises and detained. The protesters had sought a meeting with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the other Election Commissioners to raise their concerns over the SIR exercise. The INDIA bloc march began from Parliament at around 10.30 am and proceeded towards Nirvachan Sadan, the ECI headquarters. Police stopped the protesters near the NITI Aayog office using barricades. According to Delhi Police, the protesters had not been granted permission for the march. Police said the protesters breached the first barricade and continued towards a second one despite repeated announcements asking them to disperse. Around 260 people, including 10 MPs, were detained during the protest, police said. As the march was stopped, Rahul Gandhi climbed onto a police barricade and waved the national flag. Priyanka Gandhi was initially taken to a waiting police bus but got off and joined her brother near the Akashvani Bhawan gate. Rahul, Priyanka and Congress MP Deepender Hooda subsequently entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises through the reception gate. Akashvani staff and security personnel attempted to stop them, but the leaders entered the premises and began a sit-in. They were later joined by Congress leaders including KC Venugopal and Pawan Khera, while several other Opposition MPs and leaders reached the premises. Trinamool Congress leaders Derek O’Brien and Mahua Moitra also joined the demonstration. items.title: Voter turnout in TN’s Madurantakam and Dharapuram bye-polls drop
items.summary: Voter turnout in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies in Tamil Nadu dipped significantly in the bye-elections held on October 6, compared to the Assembly polls five months ago. According to the figures reported by the Election Commission of India (ECI) website at 9 pm on the day, Madurantakam recorded an approximate turnout of 86.26%, against 93.22% in the Assembly election, with a drop of nearly 7%. Dharapuram recorded 80.30% polling, compared to 89.89% in the Assembly election, indicating a decline of nearly 9.5 percent The bye-elections were necessitated after the sitting MLAs, who had won the seats on All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) tickets in the Assembly election, subsequently switched to the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). For the bye-elections, TVK fielded the same two candidates. The bye-elections were held as a five-cornered contest between the ruling TVK, Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), AIADMK, and Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK). Left parties, despite their post-poll alliance with the TVK, fielded their own candidates. A Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] candidate contested in Madurantakam and the Communist Party of India (CPI) candidate contested in Dharapuram. Madurantakam Polling in Madurantakam, a reserved constituency in Chengalpattu district, was largely peaceful, despite a few reported glitches involving Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs). At booth number 26 in Sithandi, the EVM’s control unit reportedly malfunctioned and had to be replaced twice, delaying the start of polling. At booth number 55 in Endathur, the ballot unit was reportedly replaced after polling agents objected to a mark visible on a candidate's name. TVK candidate Maragatham Kumaravel, who had earlier won the seat as an AIADMK candidate, dismissed allegations that her party had distributed money to voters. "TVK's policy is to provide a corruption-free and clean administration. How can people like us give money for votes? We have not given even one rupee. items.title: Kerala HC orders CBI probe into 14-yr-old disappearance of Tripura Rifles jawan
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has ordered a CBI investigation into the disappearance of a Tripura State Rifles jawan who went missing during a train journey from Kerala to Guwahati in April 2012, observing that the case was among the “rarest”, warranting the exercise of the court’s constitutional powers even after 14 years. Justice G Girish, in a judgment delivered on September 29, directed the CBI to take over the investigation into the disappearance of Subash Chandra Bose P, Rifle Man No. 06110758 of the Third Battalion, Tripura State Rifles. The court opened its judgment by underscoring the responsibility owed to soldiers, observing: “Peaceful sleep of the civilian is at the cost of sleepless nights, vigilance and sacrifice of the soldier.” It added that civilian society “owes a responsibility to stand by the soldier who protects them, in case he faces a crisis in personal life.” Subash had gone missing on April 4, 2012, while travelling by train from Kerala to Guwahati after spending a month-long leave at his native place in Vengoor, Ernakulam. His father, PK Balan, had seen him off at Ernakulam railway station on April 3. The next day, Balan received a call from an unfamiliar number. His son reportedly said that the train had reached Visakhapatnam and that he was unwell, but assured his father that he could take care of himself and travel to Tripura, where he was posted. On April 10, however, the Commandant of the Tripura State Rifles informed Balan that his son had not reported for duty after his leave. Balan approached the Railway Police in Ernakulam on April 13 and subsequently contacted several authorities, including police officials in Agartala and Kerala, and the Union Ministry of Home Affairs. He eventually approached the High Court in October 2012 seeking directions to trace his son. The High Court had earlier directed the Kerala police to ascertain the action taken by the Railway Police in Visakhapatnam. The Visakhapatnam police later closed the investigation as undetected, while the Tripura State Rifles also failed to make a breakthrough. Opposing a CBI probe, the agency's Special Public Prosecutor argued that the Kerala High Court lacked territorial jurisdiction since the disappearance could have occurred between Visakhapatnam and Guwahati. The CBI also contended that after 14 years, there was little possibility of tracing the missing man or gathering information about his disappearance. The court rejected both objections. items.title: Hyderabad BJP BLA booked over attempt to delete 30 Muslim voters using Form 7
items.summary: A BJP booth-level agent, S Balachander, has been booked in Hyderabad for allegedly attempting to delete 30 Muslim voters from the electoral rolls using pre-printed Form 7 applications. The Chikkadpally police registered the case on October 6 after election officials found that all 30 voters were living at the addresses recorded in the electoral rolls. The case was based on a complaint by T Praveen Kumar, Electoral Registration Officer of the Musheerabad Assembly constituency and Deputy Commissioner of GHMC Circle 41. Police booked Balachander under sections 217 (false information with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to the injury of another person) and 318(2) (cheating) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. According to the complaint, Balachander brought 30 digitally pre-printed Form 7 applications to polling station No. 210 in Surya Nagar, Chikkadpally, on September 28. The applications, which were signed by Balachander, sought deletion of the names of 30 electors from the rolls. As TNM previously reported , some of the individuals Balachander submitted Form 7 applications against were known to him for years. The Booth Level Officer (BLO) and polling station supervisor refused to accept the bulk submission despite repeated requests and did not issue an acknowledgement. Balachander allegedly left the forms at the polling station and left the premises. The BLO and supervisor subsequently conducted a field verification on September 30 and submitted their report. On October 1, the Assistant ERO and ERO joined the verification of all 30 voters. Officials found that 14 of the electors were registered at one address and the remaining 16 at another. All 30 were found residing at the respective addresses recorded in the electoral rolls. Based on the verification, election officials concluded that the Form 7 applications were not maintainable and were liable to be rejected. The case comes amid a wider controversy over the misuse of Form 7 applications during special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharshan Reddy had earlier said disputed Form 7 applications submitted in Musheerabad and Goshamahal constituencies had been rejected. items.title: NHAI floats Rs 11538 crore tenders for Amaravati Outer Ring Road
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has invited bids for the construction of the proposed six-lane, access-controlled Amaravati Outer Ring Road (ORR), with the 195.23-km project divided into four packages under the Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM). The tenders, issued on October 2, carry a combined estimated cost of Rs 11,537.70 crore. Each package has a construction schedule of 1,095 days, or three years. Bidders must submit their offers by 11 am on November 18, with the bids scheduled to be opened the following day. The first package covers the 27.93-km stretch between Kanchikacherla and Nandigama at an estimated cost of Rs 2,975.47 crore. Package 2, the longest at 56 km, will connect Nandigama with Davuluru and has been pegged at Rs 2,864.69 crore. The third package, estimated at Rs 2,827.95 crore, covers 55.80 km between Kolavennu and Kornepadu. It also includes a 5.3-km spur connecting the ORR to Narakoduru. The final package spans 55.50 km from Kornepadu to Kanchikacherla and is estimated to cost Rs 2,869.59 crore. Once completed, the ring road is expected to provide a high-capacity alternative for traffic around the Amaravati-Vijayawada-Guntur region with an aim to improving connectivity for commuters and freight operators. The tender process has been initiated ahead of the project's formal approval by the Union Cabinet, with the government seeking to prevent procedural delays. Union Minister of State for Rural Development Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar stated that the proposal was under active consideration and would be placed before the Cabinet after receiving the Finance department's clearance. items.title: Kerala HC denies anticipatory bail to man accused of deceiving Dalit woman for sex
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has refused anticipatory bail to a 39-year-old man accused of concealing his existing relationship and three-year-old child before fixing his marriage with a Dalit woman, holding that the alleged conduct prima facie amounts to sexual intercourse by deceitful means under section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Justice A Badharudee, on September 28, dismissed the appeal filed by Udayan, the first accused in a case registered at Feroke police station in Kozhikode, and directed him to surrender before the investigating officer. The court said that if he failed to surrender, the investigating officer was at liberty to arrest him and proceed with the investigation. items.summary: Nandini milk is set to become costlier by up to Rs 8 per litre after the Karnataka Cabinet approved a price hike on October 6, but held back its announcement due to the Model Code of Conduct (MCC). The government will seek the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) approval before implementing the hike, with Chief Minister DK Shivakumar authorised to take the final call on the extent of the increase. The revised prices are likely to come into effect from November 1, subject to ECI clearance. If the full Rs 8 increase is passed on to consumers, Nandini toned milk, sold in the blue packet, will cost Rs 54 per litre, up from the current Rs 46. Of the proposed Rs 8 increase, Rs 6 is expected to go to milk producers and Rs 2 to milk unions. The hike comes after milk unions sought an increase of Rs 8 to Rs 10 per litre, citing rising costs of cattle feed, fodder, medicines, transportation and plastic packaging. They also pointed to fodder shortages caused by the drought and Karnataka’s lower milk procurement price compared to neighbouring states. According to the unions, toned milk is procured at Rs 35 per litre in Karnataka, compared to Rs 41.50 in Andhra Pradesh, Rs 41.80 in Kerala, Rs 41 in Maharashtra and Rs 42.24 in Tamil Nadu. The proposed increase would be the fifth revision in Nandini milk prices since November 2022. Prices were increased by Rs 3 per litre in November 2022, another Rs 3 in July 2023, Rs 2 in June 2024 and Rs 4 in March 2025. In June 2024, consumers were given an additional 50 ml of milk for every litre following the price increase. The Karnataka Milk Federation later withdrew the additional quantity.
